account: Warwickshire County Council tested a locally hosted Llama 2 model that classified businesses by size and food availability. The council aimed to identify areas with limited access to affordable, nutritious food. Accuracy was 63%, compared with 95% for a simpler method. Processing took up to 1.5 hours per output. In its case study, the Local Government Association reports that the model added irrelevant text to 3.8 percent of its answers and that eight answers included business names. The association describes those names as a potential security risk. Inconsistent model labels in the case study leave the exact configuration unclear. The council anticipated that further fine-tuning could save staff time on manual searches. Its evaluation demonstrates neither time savings nor improved food access. According to a separate cost analysis, dedicated hardware for large language models would be expensive, with a used graphics card costing about £41,000. The association closes with the note that the council continued to explore cheaper ways to run large language models in-house.

ai_role.statement: The council compared the prompted LLM with a rule-based method on the same task, and the method without AI was more accurate. The LLM also produced irrelevant output in 3.8 percent of cases, and eight responses included business names. Any staff-time saving remains a forecast that depends on further fine-tuning.
